items.title: Juxtaposing an H1-regular sequence with an H1-regular sequence modulo the ideal it generates stays H1-regular
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the gluing statement for H_1-regularity: if I is generated by an H_1-regular sequence f_1 to f_n and the images of g_1 to g_m are H_1-regular in A/I, then the juxtaposed sequence f_1 to f_n, g_1 to g_m is H_1-regular in A (statement lines 7575-7582). Its proof is a 32-line argument built on a commutative diagram of the two Koszul complexes (proof lines 7585-7616) and it proceeds in two genuine correction steps: an element of A^{n+m} mapping to zero is first corrected by lifting an element of the exterior square from A/I to A so that its last m coordinates land in I, and then corrected along the images of the wedge elements (0, ..., g_j, 0, ..., f_i, 0, ...) so that those coordinates become zero; what remains lies in the first n coordinates and dies by the assumed H_1-regularity of f_1 to f_n. The case in which the two sequences interact is exactly the content of the lemma, and neither correction is bookkeeping.
